issues.note: Real points (adverb example, sense 4 overlap) but quotes sense 2 definition, muddled reasoning.
Leave something behind is the adverb, not this preposition.
'in the behind position' is not natural English.
Adverb use with no object; belongs to the adverb entry.
Same unnatural example; it needs rewriting.
Doubtful error; 'behind the schedule' is likelier. Not clearly invented.
sb/sth abbreviations are banned in prose.
Keyword rule puts the idiom under the noun back, not behind.
Wording is slightly odd for figurative support; minor taste point.
Cannot replace behind in examples; 'supports' duplicates sense 3.

findings.F1: Sense 1 example 'located in the behind position of the store' is unnatural English.
findings.F2: Adverb use 'He left his keys behind' appears as an example of the preposition.
findings.F3: Sense 3 definition uses the banned abbreviations sb and sth.
findings.F4: Sense 4 definition is not substitutable and overlaps sense 3 with 'supports'.
